When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **3/10**, WARNING (price damage still limited) vs VIX Spike tier **4/4** EXTREME, **85%** probability
The Crash Index counts stress that has already hit prices, while the VIX detector prices what options traders expect next. Trust the VIX tier for risk sizing, because the options market moves first and the crash score catches up later.
⚠ These two disagree: VIX backwardation active (short term fear above long term) vs **0** of **3** confluences active (no confirmation from credit, small caps or yen)
The stress sits in index volatility alone and has not spread to other markets. Trust the missing confirmation for how aggressively you act, but treat it as a delay and keep the hedge.
⚠ These two disagree: Divergence composite in TOPPING zone, **72%** of pairs diverging vs Contrarian score **45**, ACCUMULATE (partial signal)
The buy signal is only half formed and describes a dip, while the divergence picture describes weak internal structure. Trust the topping read for sizing and add only in small steps.

Bull

Bear

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is split between a calm surface and a nervous options book. The Crash Index reads 3/10, the regime state scores 60 (TRANSITION, MIXED bias), and the VIX Spike detector sits at tier 4/4 with an 85% probability. The Nasdaq 100 is up +2.9% over 5 days while the Dow is up only +0.3%, so the gains are narrow.

That shapes positioning. The macro regime reads CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence, and the contrarian score of 45 says dip buying is only partly justified. You hold core exposure but stop adding to the leaders, and you keep protection on while backwardation is active. Buy weakness only in small tranches, and only where a name has not been part of the 72% of pairs now diverging.

The main risk is that the options market is right and the crash signals are late. Seven of the ten crash signals are still quiet, which leaves room for a fast move. The read flips toward risk off if any of the three VIX confluences (credit, small caps, yen) turns on. It flips toward risk on if the VIX term structure drops out of backwardation while the Nasdaq 100 keeps its +2.9% gain.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together have started to move apart. Correlation drift is the measured change in how tightly they move together, comparing an older window with a recent one. The composite zone is TOPPING, with 72% of 43 pairs diverging, 29 bearish and 2 bullish, and the jaws score is 100. That says the internal structure of the market is breaking up while the index looks fine.

The top pairs all score 80 (DEEP DIVERG). Regional banks against financials (KRE and XLF) moved from +0.23 to -0.68, so the weak part of banking is separating from the big banks. Visa and Mastercard flipped from +0.78 to -0.69, which is unusual for two businesses that share the same drivers. Low volatility stocks against the S&P 500 (USMV and SPY) moved from -0.94 to -0.04, so the usual hedge pattern is fading. The bond volatility index (MOVE) went from +0.28 to -0.36, and AUD/JPY went from +0.39 to -0.19. A topping zone does not give a date, but it tells you to trim the weakest links and demand more from every new position.

AI read · what the confluences mean now

No confluence is active today. VIX backwardation fires alone, and it has no support from credit stress (HYG), small cap drawdown (B2) or yen safe haven flow (JPY). That means the fear is confined to index options and has not reached funding markets or the riskier parts of equities.

You lean cautious and wait for proof, and you don't add risk because of a single gauge. Keep hedges in place while backwardation lasts. Watch the three confluence lines each day, since the first one to switch on is the cue to cut exposure instead of just holding protection.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is narrow and uneven. Asia is split, with the Nikkei at +6.2% over 5 days and the Shanghai Composite at -2.8%. Europe is weak, with the DAX at -0.5% and the CAC 40 at -3.0%. The US shows the Nasdaq 100 at +2.9% and the Dow at +0.3%. In crypto, SOL leads at +1.8% and ETH trails at -0.3%.

That points to a US session driven by large technology leaders, with cyclicals and Europe offering little support. The Japan strength and the Nasdaq strength fit the same risk on pocket, while the French and Chinese weakness shows the rest of the world is not joining in. Expect the Nasdaq 100 to carry the index and watch the Dow for confirmation. If the Dow keeps stalling near +0.3%, the VIX stress gets more credible.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The two gauges disagree, and that is a coherent state. The Crash Index at 3/10 measures damage that has already shown up in prices and breadth. The VIX Spike detector at tier 4/4 (EXTREME, 85% probability) measures what options traders are paying to protect against. Skew, backwardation and the adaptive trigger are all active, so traders are bidding for near term protection even though price action is orderly.

Trust the VIX tier for sizing, because options reprice before stocks do. The Crash Index is the lagging confirmation, and it already sits in WARNING at 3 signals. Another signal or two turning on would close the gap from the price side. A drop in the VIX tier would close it from the other side.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
